children: The relative performance of semiconductor stocks versus the S&P 500 has weakened sharply, with the 100-day spread falling below its 20-year average, according to Daily Chartbook.

“At the start of the month, the 100-day relative spread between semiconductors and the S&P 500 was falling from its extreme relative momentum reading in May,” Daily Chartbook said in a post on X. “Today, the spread has fallen below its 20-year average.”
The chart tracks the 100-day trailing relative return spread between the VanEck Semiconductor ETF
from 2006 through 2026. The spread measures how semiconductor stocks have performed relative to the broader S&P 500 over the preceding 100 trading days.
The spread had climbed to more than 60% earlier in 2026, its highest level on the chart, before retreating sharply. The latest reading was close to 0% and had moved below the long-term average.
The chart also showed several previous periods when the spread moved well above or below its historical average, including sharp swings during 2008-09, 2020-22, and 2024-25.

title: Semiconductor relative momentum falls below 20-year average
